title: Fort Worth, Texas
wiki_lead:
Fort Worth is a city in the U.S. state of Texas. It is the county seat of Tarrant County, covering nearly 350 square miles (910 km2) and extending into Denton, Johnson, Parker, and Wise counties. Fort Worth's population was estimated to be 1,028,117 in 2025, making it the 10th-most populous city in the United States. Fort Worth is the second-largest city in the Dallas–Fort Worth metroplex (after Dallas) and the fourth-most populous in Texas. The Dallas–Fort Worth metroplex is the fourth-most populous metropolitan area in the U.S., with 8.5 million residents.
The city of Fort Worth was established in 1849 as an army outpost on a bluff overlooking the Trinity River. Fort Worth has historically been a center of the Texas Longhorn cattle trade. It still embraces its Western heritage and traditional architecture and design. USS Fort Worth (LCS-3) is the first ship of the United States Navy named after the city. Nearby Dallas has held a population majority in the metropolitan area for as long as records have been kept, yet Fort Worth has become one of the fastest-growing cities in the United States.
The city is the location of the Van Cliburn International Piano Competition and several museums designed by contemporary architects. The Kimbell Art Museum was designed by Louis Kahn, with an addition designed by Renzo Piano. The Modern Art Museum of Fort Worth was designed by Tadao Ando. The Amon Carter Museum of American Art, designed by Philip Johnson, houses American art. The Sid Richardson Museum, redesigned by David M. Schwarz, has a collection of Western art in the United States emphasizing Frederic Remington and Charles Russell. The Fort Worth Museum of Science and History was designed by Ricardo Legorreta of Mexico.
In addition, Fort Worth is the location of several universities, including the University of Texas at Arlington, Texas Christian University, Texas Wesleyan University, UNT Health Fort Worth, and Texas A&M University School of Law. Several multinational corporations, including Bell Textron, American Airlines, and BNSF Railway, are headquartered in Fort Worth.

History

The Treaty of Bird's Fort between the Republic of Texas and several Native American tribes was signed in 1843 at Bird's Fort in present-day Arlington, Texas. Article XI of the treaty provided that no one may "pass the line of trading houses" (at the border of the Indians' territory) without permission of the President of Texas, and may not reside or remain in the Indians' territory. These "trading houses" were later established at the junction of the Clear Fork and West Fork of the Trinity River in present-day Fort Worth.
A line of seven army posts was established in 1848–1849 after the Mexican War to protect the settlers of Texas along the western American Frontier and included Fort Worth, Fort Graham, Fort Gates, Fort Croghan, Fort Martin Scott, Fort Lincoln, and Fort Duncan. grok_lead: Fort Worth is a city in North Texas, United States, and the county seat of Tarrant County. As of July 1, 2024, its population stood at 1,008,106, making it the eleventh-most populous city in the country and the fifth-largest in Texas. Established in 1849 as a U.S. Army outpost to guard the Texas frontier against Native American raids, the settlement was named in honor of General William Jenkins Worth and grew rapidly with the arrival of railroads and cattle drives in the late 19th century. Known as "Cowtown" for its pivotal role in the cattle industry, Fort Worth adopted the motto "Where the West Begins" to reflect its position as a gateway to the American West. The city's economy originated in ranching, agriculture, and oil extraction but evolved significantly after World War II into a hub for aviation, aerospace manufacturing, and defense industries, bolstered by the presence of major employers like Lockheed Martin and Bell Helicopter. Today, Fort Worth forms a core part of the Dallas âFort Worth metropolitan area, one of the fastest-growing regions in the U.S., with a diversified economy encompassing finance, logistics, and healthcare alongside its preserved western heritage sites like the Fort Worth Stockyards. Culturally, it distinguishes itself from neighboring Dallas through institutions such as the Kimbell Art Museum and a commitment to cowboy traditions, including twice-daily cattle drives that attract tourists and underscore its historical identity. Despite rapid urbanization, Fort Worth maintains lower density and a more conservative political orientation compared to Dallas, contributing to its appeal as a center for energy independence and manufacturing innovation in Texas.
